subject: ClearWave integration: SDK runway, endpoint migration & retry guidance

Subject: Next steps after demo — SDK + integration questions

Thanks again for the demo today — very helpful. Tom and I went through the recording and we have a few concrete asks to kick off our implementation sprint: 

1) ClearWave would like a short SDK quickstart (Node + Python) with a working sample that wires up our existing request flow.
2) We need guidance for endpoint migration (we're currently using /v1/generate on an older endpoint) — what are the minimal changes to switch to Redwood's streaming endpoint and keep our latency profile?
3) Retry/backoff recommendations and any recommended timeout defaults for healthcare workloads (we have strict SLA windows).

I've attached a very rough mutual action plan (ClearWave-MAP.xlsx) and our network requirements doc so you can flag any networking constraints. Can we aim to have a tech handoff and a short implementation guide by next Tuesday?

Appreciate it —

Subject: Re: Next steps after demo — SDK + integration questions

Hi Aisha — great meeting earlier. We're aligned on the deliverables and can get a concise tech runway document to you by Tue 4/17. High-level notes here so your engineers can start experimenting immediately: 

1) SDK quickstarts (what to expect)
- We'll include: auth pattern, streaming vs non-streaming call, example retries, and graceful cancellation.
- Official SDKs: @redwood/js (Node 18+), @redwood/py (3.10+). Both include built-in retry helpers.

2) Endpoint migration notes (minimal changes)
- Current (your code): POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate with a JSON body {"prompt": "...", "max_tokens": 512}.
- Target (streaming, lower tail latency): POST https://inference-us.redwood.ai/v1/stream with same JSON shape but set "stream": true. If you need chunked processing, consume server-sent-events (SSE) or WebSocket stream depending on SDK and runtime.
- Token/auth: Use Authorization: Bearer <API_KEY>. Avoid embedding keys in client-side code — put in server-side env variables.

3) Retries, timeouts, and idempotency
- Recommended pattern: idempotency key + exponential backoff with jitter. Example policy: 
  * Retries: 3 attempts max for 5xx and network errors
  * Backoff: base = 200ms, factor = 2, jitter = random(0, 100ms) => 200ms, 400ms, 800ms
  * For 429: read Retry-After header and wait that duration; if absent, use 1s + exponential backoff.
- Timeout defaults: set client-level request timeout = 60s for non-streaming generation; streaming connections: keep-alive 120s and implement reconnect with resume semantics where possible (we'll include KV cache resumption notes).

4) Rate limits
- Default per-tenant soft limit: 120 requests/min (configurable for enterprise). When you see HTTP 429, follow the Retry-After header. We recommend client-side token bucket throttling to smooth bursts.

I'll attach a short sample file (redwood-sdk-sample-snippets.txt) in the formal doc. Below is a tiny Node snippet to get you started — this uses our JS SDK and shows streaming handling: 

// Node example (pseudo-code)
import Redwood from '@redwood/js';
const client = new Redwood({ apiKey: process.env.REDWOOD_KEY, baseURL: 'https://inference-us.redwood.ai' });

// streaming call
const stream = await client.stream({ model: 'rw-2028-base', prompt: 'Summarize patient visit notes.', stream: true });
stream.on('data', chunk => {
  // chunk.delta contains token text
  process.stdout.write(chunk.delta || '');
});
stream.on('end', () => console.log('
--done--'));

On retries, the SDK exposes client.withRetries({ attempts: 3, backoffBaseMs: 200 }). We'll include a short table of what errors we retry vs what we surface to the app.

If your infra team can share any proxy / egress constraints from the network_requirements.pdf, we can call out special headers or TLS cipher recommendations.

I'll follow up with a link to the GH gist and the handoff doc by Friday. If anyone on your eng team wants an office hours slot, book here: https://cal.redwood.ai/ben/30min

Thanks,
Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Aisha — Monica here from Customer Success. A couple of practical notes for your PM/ops team: 

- Canary plan: we advise a 2-stage rollout — (1) 5% of traffic for 48 hours, (2) 25% for 72 hours, then full. We'll provide a short script to toggle weights via the console API.
- Observability: enable request-level tracing headers (X-Request-ID) and forward any 5xx/429 samples to our support channel for quicker debug.
- Security: if you require VPC peering or private endpoints, mention that as early as possible; those add ~4 weeks to schedule.

Quick cURL sample for non-streaming generation (for your test harness):

curl -sS -X POST \
  'https://inference-us.redwood.ai/v1/generate' \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"rw-2028-base","prompt":"Extract diagnosis codes from: <text>","max_tokens":256}'

We'll include a small config template with recommended timeouts and retry header handling in the doc I attach. Marissa will own the MAP updates and the meeting invites.

Best,
Monica Patel
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@clearwavehealth.com>

Date: Thu, 12 Apr 2028 11:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps after demo — SDK + integration questions

Thanks Ben/Monica — this is excellent. A few follow-ups from Tom and our infra lead: 

- Latency constraints: for some flows we need p95 < 250ms and p99 < 600ms end-to-end (including our network hop). Do you have recommended model/config combos we should target to meet those numbers?
- Resilience: if streaming connection drops, can we resume or do we need to re-issue the request and stitch results?
- Compliance/question: will audit logs include per-request user identity and raw prompts? We need this for our audit trail.

If you can call out any recommended model sizes (quantized variants) and how they affect both latency and cost that would help our cost model. Also please confirm whether the 120 req/min default is per-API-key or per-tenant.

On the timeline: getting private endpoints would be preferred but if it adds 4 weeks we might proceed with public endpoint + VPC peering later.

On the attached MAP we've added a row for 'compliance evidence' — Monica, can you own that?

Thanks,
Aisha

From: ben_carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Shah <aisha.shah@clearwavehealth.com>
Cc: monica_patel <monica.patel@redwood.ai>, marissa_cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 Apr 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps after demo — SDK + integration questions

Aisha / Tom — responses inline and next steps: 

- Latency & model guidance: for p95~250ms you should target a smaller, optimized model variant (rw-2028-small-quant) with sequence length tuned to the task (we recommend max_tokens <= 256 for extraction flows). We'll include perf numbers in the doc (baseline: rw-2028-small-quant ~ p95 180ms, p99 ~ 420ms in our us-west region under steady load).

- Resume semantics: currently we do not support byte-level resume on stream drops. Best practice: assign an idempotency_key per logical request and re-issue request on reconnect; use partial-result heuristics to stitch if you maintain server-side offsets. We'll add a small client helper to detect duplicate partials.

- Audit logs: yes — for enterprise tenants we can surface per-request metadata (request_id, user_id if forwarded, timestamp) and store raw prompt blobs in audit storage per your retention policy. We'll document retention options and compliance export process (SOC2 evidence is available). Monica to own compliance evidence coordination.

- Rate limit scope: default soft-limit is per-tenant. If you need per-api-key partitioning we'll propose a scoped quota mapping in the Dedicated/Private contract.

Action items: 
- Ben: deliver SDK quickstart + code snippets (by 2028-04-20) — done (attached).
- Marissa: update MAP with rollout dates and meeting cadence (by 2028-04-18).
- Monica: start compliance evidence checklist and open a ticket for audit log export (by 2028-04-19).

Link to the shared handoff doc: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1X-demo-runway-plan
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/1234567/deal/458

I'll schedule a 30min office hours for next Tue to walk the engs through the sample code. Thanks all — looking forward to the rollout.

Cheers,
Ben Carter
